name: TX-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with an R+11 partisan lean
Incumbent Craig Goldman running with a large cash advantage ($1.5M on hand)
Prediction markets price Goldman at ~95% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean, Goldman's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and markets pricing him near 95% all point to a comfortable Republican hold, with no polling or ratings suggesting a competitive race.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or a dramatically favorable national environment for Democrats could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-12 is a solidly Republican Fort Worth-area district, and first-term incumbent Craig Goldman is seeking reelection with a substantial financial edge. He has raised about $1.8 million and holds roughly $1.5 million on hand, while Democrat Angela Rodriguez Prilliman has reported little visible fundraising or outside support. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and market pricing.

Prediction markets give Goldman about a 95% chance of winning, consistent with the district's Republican lean and his incumbency. The forecast expects Goldman to win by roughly fifteen points, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling. A Democratic upset would require an unusual late shift in the national environment or an unexpected development in the race.
